release_notes: **AI assistants can save and edit strategy specs** through the MCP server: new `get_strategy_spec` (always available) and `save_strategy_spec` tools, behind a new off-by-default Settings switch (Settings → Safety → "Allow AI assistant (MCP) to save and edit strategy specs"). New names save directly, left disabled and paper. Overwriting an existing strategy is refused unless it is disarmed, disabled and flat, previews the changes first (two calls), keeps the previous version as `<name>.spec.json.bak`, and logs the diff in the event log with `source: mcp`. The `thetaprime-strategy-builder` skill uses them when present and falls back to file/paste otherwise (reinstall the skill from Composer to pick this up). See `docs/mcp-setup.md`. MCP tool errors from `/composer/*` now show the validation messages instead of a bare "400 Client Error". **`enable_strategy` / `disable_strategy` MCP tools**. Enabling needs the existing "Allow AI assistant (MCP) to arm, enable and square off strategies" switch, is refused while the daily loss limit is active, and for a real-mode strategy is two calls (the first returns mode, armed state and next entry time). Disabling is ungated but refused unless the strategy is flat. Both log `source: mcp`; the dashboard toggle is unchanged. An unknown strategy name is a 404 instead of creating an orphan metadata entry. **Composer overwrite left a running engine on the old spec**: saving over an existing strategy from Composer now resets its running PositionEngine, like every other config change. **Disarmed real strategy could place live entries**: a real-mode strategy that was enabled but only disarmed (dashboard Disarm, MCP `disarm_strategy`, loss-limit breach) had its monitor ticks exempt from the arm gate, and the monitor retries entry on every tick while flat -- so it could open a live position. Monitor ticks (ephemeral and PositionEngine) now block new entries for an unarmed real strategy; exits and management of an already-open position are unchanged. Production (non-dev) only, where the arm gate applies. **Torn spec files**: Composer saves write both files to temp paths and swap them in, so a failed write can't leave a truncated spec or a spec/sidecar mismatch. **Disabling, deleting or archiving a strategy unscheduled similarly named ones**: `foo` also removed `foo_v2`'s jobs (job ids were prefix-matched). They are now matched exactly. **Breeze burned its daily API-call cap (3,500) by 11:27, leaving a live position with no prices and no event-log entry** (2026-09-21, again after 2026-09-18): `BreezeAdapter.ltp()` only read the WebSocket tick cache when the ticker was "verified", and that flag lived in the main app process only -- PositionEngines and strategy runs are subprocesses, so they always went to REST. The verified flag is now published beside the tick cache (10-minute TTL, fail-safe off, heartbeated while verified), and cached ticks are trusted by feed liveness: while the NIFTY spot row is at most 5s old, any leg row up to 90s old is served (a quiet leg is still at its last traded price), otherwise only rows at most 3s old. Measured on a live 7-leg position: 17/20 polls hit REST with the old fixed 3s window, 0/20 with this. **Breeze quota and pricing-blind-spot alerts**: one alert a day when ThetaPrime's own cap trips, one a day when ICICI returns its daily-quota rejection (the old "15 hits in 120s" alert could never fire for it), and one per 30 minutes when legs cannot be priced while REST is blocked -- the engine then holds each leg at its last mark, still labelled live, so stop-losses are not being evaluated on fresh prices. De-duplicated across strategy subprocesses. **Alerts and event-log writes failed silently**: `log_event`, `get_events`, `cleanup_old_events` and `Resilience.alert` swallowed every exception, so a locked `performance.db` lost alerts with no trace. They still never raise, but now log the failure (and the full lost event) to the app log. **Test suite could send real alerts**: `import app` under pytest started a real Dhan price feed on the developer machine's stored (stale) token when `brokers.dhan.ws_ticks` was on, which sent a genuine "Dhan session expired" alert to WhatsApp and Telegram. `tests/conftest.py` now disables it like the Kite and Breeze feeds. No effect on installed builds. Needs a full rebuild + reinstall (app, spec, scheduler, strategy_manager and the broker adapters are compiled); `mcp_server.py` ships as plain source.
